bank.name: Foreign Policy
bank.subject: Pakistan Affairs
bank.description: Pakistan's relations with international organisations and major powers, and its key foreign policy milestones.

questions.prompt: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined the United Nations on 30 September 1947.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) founded, with Pakistan as a founding member?
questions.explanation: The OIC was founded at the 1969 Rabat summit; Pakistan hosted its second summit in Lahore in 1974.

questions.prompt: In which year was SAARC founded, and where is its headquarters?
questions.explanation: SAARC was founded in 1985 at the Dhaka summit; its secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal.

questions.prompt: Pakistan left the Commonwealth in 1972 and rejoined in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan withdrew from the Commonwealth in 1972 and rejoined in 1989.

questions.prompt: Pakistan was among the first countries to recognize the People's Republic of China, doing so in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan recognised the PRC in 1950, and formal diplomatic relations were established in 1951.

questions.prompt: In which year did Pakistan join SEATO?
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) in 1954.

questions.prompt: Where is the headquarters of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
questions.explanation: The ECO, established in 1985 as the successor of RCD, has its secretariat in Tehran.

questions.prompt: The D-8 (Developing Eight) organisation was founded in which year and city?
questions.explanation: The D-8 was founded in 1997 in Istanbul; Pakistan is a founding member.

questions.prompt: In which year did Pakistan become a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
questions.explanation: Pakistan and India were admitted as full SCO members at the Astana summit in June 2017.

questions.prompt: The first war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir was fought in which year?
questions.explanation: The first Kashmir war was fought in 1947-48, ending with a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1949.

questions.prompt: The Line of Control (LOC) in Kashmir was formalised under which agreement?
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement (1972) converted the 1949 ceasefire line into the Line of Control.

questions.prompt: Which country is called Pakistan's 'all-weather friend'?
questions.explanation: China is widely referred to as Pakistan's all-weather friend and iron brother.

questions.prompt: Which country does Pakistan NOT share a border with?
questions.explanation: Turkey does not share a land border with Pakistan.

questions.prompt: The Baghdad Pact, later renamed CENTO, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact in 1955, renamed CENTO after Iraq's withdrawal.

questions.prompt: Pakistan left SEATO and CENTO in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan withdrew from both pacts in 1972 under Bhutto's foreign policy.

questions.prompt: Pakistan recognized the independence of which Central Asian states in 1991?
questions.explanation: Pakistan recognized all five Central Asian republics after the USSR dissolved in 1991.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's longest border is with which country?
questions.explanation: The border with India (including Kashmir) is Pakistan's longest.

questions.prompt: The 'Agreement on Bilateral Cooperation' signed by Pakistan and China in 2020 extended the friendship to how many years?
questions.explanation: In 2020, Pakistan and China agreed to extend their strategic cooperation to 80 years.

questions.prompt: Pakistan played a key role in opening US-China relations in 1971 through which diplomat?
questions.explanation: Bhutto, as foreign minister, and Yahya Khan helped arrange Kissinger's secret 1971 visit to China.

questions.prompt: Pakistan is a member of which South Asian regional organization?
questions.explanation: Pakistan is a founding member of SAARC (established 1985).

questions.prompt: The 'Zarb-e-Azb' and 'Radd-ul-Fasaad' operations were Pakistan's domestic counter-terrorism campaigns. Which statement is true?
options: They were domestic security operations, not foreign policy agreements
questions.explanation: Zarb-e-Azb (2014) and Radd-ul-Fasaad (2017) were military operations inside Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's ambassador who was martyred in the 2008 Marriott bombing in Islamabad was?
options: No ambassador was killed; the Czech ambassador's car was struck
questions.explanation: The 2008 Marriott attack killed the Czech ambassador to Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Which international event did Pakistan host in 1996?
questions.explanation: Pakistan co-hosted the 1996 Cricket World Cup with India and Sri Lanka.

questions.prompt: The 'Kartarpur Corridor' opened in 2019 connects Pakistan with India for pilgrims of which faith?
questions.explanation: The Kartarpur Corridor lets Sikh pilgrims visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib visa-free.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's first head of state was?
questions.explanation: Jinnah served as Governor-General, the head of state, from 1947 to 1948.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's permanent representative to the UN in 1947 presented the Kashmir issue; who was he?
questions.explanation: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan, foreign minister, took the Kashmir dispute to the UN in 1948.

questions.prompt: Which Pakistani served as President of the UN General Assembly?
questions.explanation: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan was UNGA President in 1962-63.

questions.prompt: Pakistan is a founding member of which Islamic body?
questions.explanation: Pakistan co-founded the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

questions.prompt: The 'Indus Waters Treaty' was signed with India in?
questions.explanation: The World Bank-brokered Indus Waters Treaty was signed on 19 September 1960.

questions.prompt: Which rivers were allocated to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty?
questions.explanation: Pakistan received the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab); India the eastern ones.

questions.prompt: Pakistan and India signed the 'Tashkent Declaration' after which war?
questions.explanation: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration ended the 1965 Indo-Pakistan war.

questions.prompt: The Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir was formalized by?
questions.explanation: The 1972 Simla Agreement converted the ceasefire line into the LoC.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's nuclear policy is described as?
questions.explanation: Pakistan maintains a doctrine of credible minimum deterrence.

questions.prompt: Pakistan has not signed which international treaty?
questions.explanation: Pakistan is not a signatory to the NPT (it joined later nuclear states like India and Israel).

questions.prompt: Pakistan's relations with which country were strained by the 'Dawn leaks' and 2019 tensions?
questions.explanation: Pakistan-India tensions spiked in 2019 after Pulwama and Balakot.

questions.prompt: The 'Gwadar-Chabahar' rivalry involves which two countries?
questions.explanation: Iran's Chabahar port competes with Pakistan's Gwadar for regional trade.

questions.prompt: Pakistan recognized the Taliban government in Afghanistan in?
options: It has not formally recognized any post-2021 government; it has de facto ties
questions.explanation: Pakistan maintained de facto engagement but did not formally recognize the Taliban regime.

questions.prompt: The 'Durand Line' was drawn by which British official?
questions.explanation: Sir Mortimer Durand demarcated the 1893 border with Afghanistan.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's 'strategic depth' concept historically related to?
questions.explanation: 'Strategic depth' was a debated doctrine involving Afghanistan's role in Pakistan's security.

questions.prompt: The 'Heart of Asia-Istanbul Process' includes Pakistan as a participant. It focuses on?
questions.explanation: The Heart of Asia process promotes Afghan-led regional cooperation.

questions.prompt: Pakistan has a 'strategic partnership' with which country in the Indian Ocean?
questions.explanation: The China-Pakistan all-weather strategic partnership is central to regional ties.

questions.prompt: Which body mediates the Indus Waters Treaty disputes?
options: The World Bank (neutral expert and court of arbitration)
questions.explanation: The World Bank facilitates dispute resolution under the treaty.

questions.prompt: The 'Kashmir dispute' was first raised at the UN by Pakistan in?

questions.prompt: Which Pakistani foreign minister is known for the 'zero problems' policy with neighbors?
options: No PM applied that phrase; it was Turkey's Ahmet Davutoglu policy
questions.explanation: 'Zero problems with neighbors' was the foreign policy of Turkish PM Davutoglu, not Pakistan's.

questions.prompt: Pakistan joined the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined NAM in 1979.

questions.prompt: Pakistan left CENTO in which year?

It was too lenient on Britain
